questions.question: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endocytosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Endocytosis** is a cellular process in which substances are brought into the cell.
 
• It involves the cell membrane folding around the desired molecules to form a vesicle that is brought into the cell.
 
• Endocytosis is crucial for the intake of nutrients and other essential molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane by diffusion.
 
• There are different types of endocytosis, including phagocytosis (ingestion of large particles) and pinocytosis (ingestion of fluids and small molecules).
 
• Endocytosis plays a significant role in cellular signaling, nutrient uptake, and immune responses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exocytosis** is the process by which cells expel materials in vesicles by fusing them with the cell membrane.
 
• **Osmosis** refers to the movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of low solute concentration to high solute concentration.
 
• **Diffusion** is the passive movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
 
• **Phagocytosis** is a type of endocytosis where the cell engulfs large particles or even whole cells, typically seen in immune cells like macrophages.
 
• **Pinocytosis** is another type of endocytosis where the cell engulfs extracellular fluid and dissolved solutes, often referred to as "cell drinking."

questions.question: 'Unbreakable' is an autobiography of _______________ published in 2013.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MC Mary Kom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **MC Mary Kom** is an Indian Olympic boxer and a six-time world champion in boxing.
 
• Her autobiography, titled "**Unbreakable**", was published in **2013**.
 
• Mary Kom is also known as "**Magnificent Mary**" for her outstanding achievements in the sport.
 
• She has been awarded the **Padma Bhushan**, **Padma Shri**, and **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna** for her contributions to Indian sports.
 
• Mary Kom's story is one of resilience and determination, inspiring many young athletes across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boxing**: A combat sport in which two people throw punches at each other for a predetermined amount of time in a boxing ring.
 
• **Olympic Boxing**: Boxing has been a part of the Olympic Games since 1904, with women’s boxing introduced in the 2012 London Olympics.
 
• **AIBA World Boxing Championships**: An annual boxing competition organized by the International Boxing Association (AIBA), where Mary Kom has won six gold medals.
 
• **Padma Awards**: Among the highest civilian awards in India, recognizing achievements in various fields including arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna**: The highest sporting honor of the Republic of India, awarded annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to recognize outstanding achievements in sports.

questions.question: In a laterite soil profile, which of the following elements is present in an excessive amount?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Laterite soils are rich in **iron and aluminum**, making them characteristic of tropical and subtropical regions.
 
• Iron content in laterite soil gives it a distinctive **reddish color**.
 
• These soils form under conditions of high rainfall and temperature, which cause intense **weathering and leaching** of silica and other minerals.
 
• Laterite soils are typically **nutrient-poor** except for iron and aluminum, making them less suitable for traditional agriculture without significant amendment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laterite Soil Formation:**

 
 
• Formed through the process of **laterization**, which involves prolonged weathering in tropical and subtropical climates.
 
• High rainfall and temperature lead to the removal of soluble minerals, leaving behind iron and aluminum oxides.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Commonly used in **building construction** due to its hardness and ability to be cut into bricks.
 
• It serves as a source of **iron ore** and is mined for its metal content.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Implications:**
 
 
• Due to the low fertility, agricultural use of laterite soil requires significant **soil amendments** like fertilizers.
 
• Crops such as tea, cashew, and coffee can be grown successfully on laterite soils with proper management.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution:**
 
 
• Laterite soils are found in regions such as **India, Africa, Brazil, and Southeast Asia**.
 
• In India, states like **Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra** have extensive laterite soil deposits.

questions.question: The Hathigumpha Inscription was inscribed in which of the following historical regions of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalinga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription is located in Udayagiri hills near Bhubaneswar in Odisha, which is part of the ancient region of Kalinga.
 
• It was inscribed by King Kharavela, the ruler of the Kalinga kingdom, in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• The inscription is carved in Brahmi script and Prakrit language.
 
• It provides a detailed account of King Kharavela's reign, military conquests, and public works.
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription is a significant archaeological and historical source for understanding the history of ancient Kalinga and early Indian epigraphy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Kharavela:**

 
 
• He was a prominent Jain king of Kalinga who ruled during the 2nd century BCE.
 
• Known for his military campaigns, cultural patronage, and public welfare activities.
 
 
 
• **Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves:**
 
 
• A complex of rock-cut caves that served as residential retreats for Jain monks.
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription is located at the entrance of one of these caves.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• An ancient script used in India, which is the ancestor of many modern Indian scripts.
 
• It was prevalent during the Maurya and Gupta periods.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit Language:**
 
 
• An ancient Indian language used in inscriptions and literature.
 
• It was widely spoken and understood in ancient India, especially in royal inscriptions.

questions.question: When was 'Nai Chetna-Pahal Badlav Ki' campaign launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tue Nov 01 2022 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Nai Chetna-Pahal Badlav Ki' campaign was launched on **November 1, 2022**.
 
• This campaign is part of a larger initiative aimed at empowering women and promoting gender equality.
 
• The campaign focuses on creating awareness about women's rights and issues related to gender-based violence.
 
• It involves various activities and programs to educate and sensitize communities, especially in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gender Equality:**

 
 
• Gender equality refers to the equal rights, responsibilities, and opportunities of women and men.
 
• It implies that the interests, needs, and priorities of both women and men are taken into consideration.
 
 
 
• **Women's Empowerment:**
 
 
• Empowerment of women involves providing them with the means to gain control over their own lives and make decisions.
 
• This includes access to education, healthcare, economic opportunities, and participation in political and social processes.
 
 
 
• **Gender-Based Violence (GBV):**
 
 
• GBV is violence directed against a person because of their gender.
 
• It includes acts that inflict physical, mental, or sexual harm or suffering, threats of such acts, coercion, and other deprivations of liberty.
 
 
 
• **Community Sensitization:**
 
 
• This involves educating and raising awareness among community members about social issues such as gender equality and GBV.
 
• The goal is to change attitudes and behaviors that perpetuate discrimination and violence against women.

questions.question: Which of the following events took place in the year 1928?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Bardoli Satyagraha** took place in the year **1928**.
 
• It was led by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who later earned the title of "Sardar" for his leadership.
 
• The movement was primarily a **non-violent campaign** against the increased tax rates imposed by the British government.
 
• The success of the Bardoli Satyagraha significantly boosted the morale of Indian farmers and contributed to the Indian independence movement.
 
• The British government eventually rolled back the increased tax rates and returned confiscated lands to the farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kakori Incident:**

 
 
• The Kakori Conspiracy was a train robbery that took place on August 9, 1925, near Kakori in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It was carried out by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) to fund their revolutionary activities against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Dandi March:**
 
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the Salt March, was led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930.
 
• It was a non-violent protest against the British salt monopoly in India.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The Kheda Satyagraha took place in 1918 in the Kheda district of Gujarat.
 
• It was led by Mahatma Gandhi to support farmers who were unable to pay taxes due to crop failure and plague.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:**
 
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• He played a crucial role in the integration of princely states into the Indian Union.

questions.question: Sachin Tendulkar scored his 100th international century against which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sachin Tendulkar scored his 100th international century against Bangladesh on **March 16, 2012**, during the Asia Cup.
 
• This milestone century was achieved at the **Shere Bangla National Stadium** in Mirpur, Dhaka.
 
• Tendulkar's 100th century included **114 runs** off 147 balls, featuring 12 boundaries and 1 six.
 
• With this century, Tendulkar became the first cricketer in history to score **100 international centuries**.
 
• The match ended with Bangladesh winning by 5 wickets, despite Tendulkar's landmark achievement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sachin Tendulkar's Career Highlights:**

 
 
• Sachin Tendulkar is widely regarded as one of the greatest batsmen in the history of cricket.
 
• He holds numerous records in both Test and One-Day International (ODI) cricket, including the most runs in both formats.
 
• He made his international debut for India at the age of 16 in a Test match against Pakistan in Karachi in 1989.
 
• Tendulkar retired from international cricket in 2013, leaving behind a legacy of extraordinary achievements.
 
 
 
• **Asia Cup 2012:**
 
 
• The Asia Cup 2012 was held in Bangladesh from March 11 to March 22.
 
• India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh competed in the tournament.
 
• Pakistan won the Asia Cup 2012, defeating Bangladesh in the final by 2 runs.
 
• Shakib Al Hasan was named the Player of the Series for his all-round performance.
 
 
 
• **Shere Bangla National Stadium:**
 
 
• The Shere Bangla National Stadium is located in Mirpur, Dhaka, Bangladesh.
 
• It is one of the premier cricket venues in Bangladesh, hosting both international and domestic matches.
 
• The stadium has a seating capacity of approximately 25,000 spectators.
 
• It is named after A.K. Fazlul Huq, a prominent Bengali political leader.
 
 
 
• **Tendulkar's Milestones:**
 
 
• Sachin Tendulkar scored his first international century against England at Old Trafford in 1990.
 
• He is the only player to have scored one hundred international centuries.
 
• He is also the first player to score a double century in an ODI, achieved against South Africa in 2010.
 
• Tendulkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2014.

questions.question: In which of the following months is the Konark Dance festival organised in Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**December**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Konark Dance Festival is held annually in December.
 
• This festival takes place at the Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It showcases classical dance forms such as Odissi, Bharatnatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, and Manipuri.
 
• The festival attracts renowned dancers and artists from across India and the world.
 
• It is organized by the Odisha Tourism Development Corporation (OTDC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating from Odisha.
 
• It is known for its fluid movements and expressive gestures.
 
• The dance is characterized by its distinct poses and intricate footwork.
 
• Odissi is performed predominantly by women, although there are male dancers as well.
 
 
 
• **Konark Sun Temple**
 
 
• The Konark Sun Temple was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
 
• It is dedicated to the Sun God and is designed in the shape of a gigantic chariot.
 
• The temple is famous for its intricate stone carvings and architectural grandeur.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the major tourist attractions in Odisha.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**
 
 
• These are landmarks or areas recognized by the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) for their cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
 
• The purpose is to safeguard and preserve these sites for future generations.
 
• India has several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, and Ajanta Caves.
 
• The Konark Sun Temple is one of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India.
 
 
 
• **Odisha Tourism Development Corporation (OTDC)**
 
 
• OTDC is a government organization responsible for promoting tourism in Odisha.
 
• It organizes various cultural festivals and events to attract tourists.
 
• OTDC provides amenities and services for tourists visiting the state.
 
• The Konark Dance Festival is one of the major events organized by OTDC.

questions.question: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly was headed by __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**JB Kripalani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **JB Kripalani** was the chairman of the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India.
 
• He played a crucial role in the formulation of the Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was formed in March 1947.
 
• JB Kripalani was a prominent leader in the Indian freedom struggle and a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The sub-committee was tasked with drafting the list of fundamental rights to be included in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly of India:**

 
 
• The Constituent Assembly was formed in December 1946 to draft the Indian Constitution.
 
• It had 389 members, including representatives from provinces and princely states.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They guarantee civil liberties such that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony.
 
• These rights include the right to equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
 
 
• **JB Kripalani:**
 
 
• Jivatram Bhagwandas Kripalani, popularly known as Acharya Kripalani, was an Indian politician and freedom fighter.
 
• He was the President of the Indian National Congress during the transfer of power in 1947.
 
• Kripalani was known for his advocacy of Gandhian principles and was a key figure in the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: Devendra Fadnavis became the ________ of the state of Maharashtra on 30th June 2022.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deputy Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Devendra Fadnavis was appointed as the Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra on 30th June 2022.
 
• He had previously served as the Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 2014 to 2019.
 
• His appointment came after the political upheaval in Maharashtra leading to the formation of a new government.
 
• Fadnavis is a senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• He is known for his administrative acumen and experience in state politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Minister of Maharashtra:**

 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government in Maharashtra.
 
• The role involves overseeing the administration and executing state policies.
 
• Maharashtra has seen various political leaders holding the position since its formation in 1960.
 
 
 
• **Political Crisis in Maharashtra 2022:**
 
 
• The political crisis involved a split within the Shiv Sena party.
 
• The crisis led to the resignation of Uddhav Thackeray as Chief Minister.
 
• A new coalition government was formed with Eknath Shinde as the Chief Minister and Devendra Fadnavis as the Deputy Chief Minister.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP):**
 
 
• The BJP is one of the two major political parties in India.
 
• It was founded in 1980 and has a significant presence across the country.
 
• The party follows the ideology of Hindutva and is known for its nationalist policies.
 
 
 
• **Role of Deputy Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Deputy Chief Minister assists the Chief Minister in administrative duties.
 
• They may also take charge of specific departments or portfolios.
 
• The position is not mandatory and depends on the state's political structure and requirements.

questions.question: National Urban Livelihood Mission (NULM) was launched in which of the following Five Year plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Twelfth Five Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Urban Livelihood Mission (NULM) was launched during the Twelfth Five Year Plan period.
 
• The Twelfth Five Year Plan covered the period from 2012 to 2017.
 
• NULM aimed to reduce poverty and vulnerability of the urban poor households by enabling them to access gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities.
 
• It focused on building strong grassroots level institutions for the urban poor, providing shelter and basic amenities, and ensuring convergence of various schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-2017)**

 
 
• The main objectives included faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth.
 
• It aimed at achieving an average growth rate of 8% during the period.
 
• Focus areas included health, education, skill development, water and sanitation, infrastructure, and rural development.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of NULM**
 
 
• Employment through Skill Training & Placement (EST&P).
 
• Social Mobilization and Institutional Development (SM&ID).
 
• Capacity Building and Training (CB&T).
 
• Support to Urban Street Vendors.
 
• Shelter for Urban Homeless.
 
 
 
• **Urban Poverty**
 
 
• Urban poverty refers to the state of individuals living in urban areas who lack access to basic services and opportunities for a decent living.
 
• It encompasses issues such as inadequate housing, lack of job opportunities, and insufficient access to healthcare and education.
 
 
 
• **Five Year Plans of India**
 
 
• The Five Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• First Five Year Plan was launched in 1951.
 
• They aimed at achieving economic growth and development through planned investments and policy interventions.

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the 'Mozart of Madras'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AR Rahman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **AR Rahman** is an acclaimed Indian composer, singer, and music producer known for his work in Indian cinema.
 
• He has won several prestigious awards including **two Academy Awards** (Oscars), **two Grammy Awards**, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe.
 
• Rahman was awarded the **Padma Bhushan**, India's third-highest civilian award, in 2010.
 
• He is often referred to as the 'Mozart of Madras' for his contributions to music, especially for blending Eastern classical music with electronic music, world music, and traditional orchestral arrangements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Life:**

 
 
• Born as A.S. Dileep Kumar on 6 January 1967 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, Rahman converted to Islam following the death of his father and changed his name to Allah Rakha Rahman.
 
 
 
• **Debut and Breakthrough:**
 
 
• Rahman made his debut as a film composer with the 1992 Tamil film 'Roja,' directed by Mani Ratnam, which earned him national recognition and numerous awards.
 
 
 
• **International Recognition:**
 
 
• His work on the score for the film 'Slumdog Millionaire' (2008) brought him international fame and several awards, including the Academy Award for Best Original Score and Best Original Song.
 
 
 
• **Philanthropy and Other Ventures:**
 
 
• Besides his musical career, Rahman has also been involved in various philanthropic activities and founded the KM Music Conservatory in Chennai to nurture young musical talents.

questions.question: Which of the following para athletes is associated with the javelin throw event?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Devendra Jhajharia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Devendra Jhajharia is a prominent Indian para-athlete specializing in the javelin throw.
 
• He has won two gold medals in the Paralympic Games, first in Athens 2004 and then in Rio 2016.
 
• Jhajharia holds the world record in the F46 category javelin throw with a distance of 63.97 meters.
 
• He is the first Indian para-athlete to win two gold medals at the Paralympics.
 
• Devendra Jhajharia has been awarded the Padma Shri and the Arjuna Award for his contributions to sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paralympic Games**:

 
 
• The Paralympic Games are a major international multi-sport event for athletes with disabilities.
 
• They are held every four years, following the Olympic Games.
 
• The first official Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960.
 
• Categories of disabilities include physical, visual, and intellectual impairments.
 
 
 
• **F46 Category**:
 
 
• The F46 category is for athletes with upper limb deficiencies, such as amputations or congenital limb deficiencies.
 
• Athletes in this category compete in events like javelin throw, shot put, and discus throw.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri**:
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India.
 
• It is awarded for distinguished contributions in various fields including art, literature, sports, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Arjuna Award**:
 
 
• The Arjuna Award is India's second highest sporting honour.
 
• It is awarded annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to recognize outstanding achievements in national sports.

questions.question: 'Bayalata' is a famous folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bayalata** is a traditional folk dance-drama from the state of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• It is a form of **open-air theatre** performed mostly in rural areas.
 
• Bayalata combines elements of **music, dance, and drama** and is often based on mythological stories and local legends.
 
• This folk art is performed during the night and can last until early morning.
 
• The performances are typically held during village festivals and special occasions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yakshagana**

 
 
• Yakshagana is another major traditional theatre form from Karnataka, known for its unique style of dance, music, and dialogue delivery.
 
• It is performed with elaborate costumes, makeup, and headgear, representing characters from Hindu epics.
 
• Yakshagana is performed in open-air theatres and temples.
 
 
 
• **Dollu Kunitha**
 
 
• Dollu Kunitha is a popular drum dance of Karnataka, performed by men with large drums tied to their waist.
 
• This dance is characterized by vigorous drum beats, synchronized group movements, and high energy.
 
• It is often performed during religious festivals and community gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Kamsale**
 
 
• Kamsale is a folk dance performed by devotees of Lord Mahadeshwara in Karnataka.
 
• The dance involves rhythmic clashing of cymbals called Kamsale and is accompanied by singing praises of the deity.
 
• It is both a religious and cultural expression, showcasing devotion and art.
 
 
 
• **Bootha Aradhane**
 
 
• Bootha Aradhane, or spirit worship, is a ritualistic folk dance from the coastal regions of Karnataka.
 
• This dance form involves invoking and appeasing local deities or spirits.
 
• It includes elaborate costumes, masks, and dramatic enactments of mythological stories.

questions.question: Which of the following States/Union Territories is NOT a part of Indus River Basin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus River Basin covers parts of India, China, and Pakistan, particularly the northern regions.
 
• States like Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, and Jammu & Kashmir are part of the Indus River Basin.
 
• Sikkim, located in the northeastern part of India, is not part of the Indus River Basin.
 
• The major rivers in Sikkim include the Teesta and Rangeet, which are part of the Brahmaputra River Basin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River Basin:**

 
 
• The Indus River originates from the Tibetan Plateau and flows through India and Pakistan.
 
• It is one of the longest rivers in the world, with a length of approximately 3,180 km.
 
• The basin covers a significant area in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The major tributaries of the Indus River include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
 
 
• **Teesta River:**
 
 
• The Teesta River is a major river in the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal.
 
• It originates from the Pahunri (or Teesta Kangse) glacier and flows southward through the Himalayas.
 
• The river ultimately merges with the Brahmaputra River in Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River Basin:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra River Basin is one of the largest river basins in the world, covering parts of China, India, and Bangladesh.
 
• It spans an area of about 580,000 square kilometers.
 
• The river is known for its strong currents and high water discharge, especially during the monsoon season.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• The Indus River Basin plays a crucial role in the agriculture and economy of the regions it covers, providing water for irrigation and drinking purposes.
 
• Sikkim, on the other hand, with its rivers like Teesta, supports hydropower projects and agricultural activities in the northeastern region of India.

questions.question: What is the chemical reaction that occurs when sugar is heated and turns into a caramel syrup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caramelisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Caramelisation** is the process of heating sugar until it breaks down and forms a deep brown, flavorful syrup.
 
• It typically occurs at temperatures between **160°C and 180°C** (320°F to 356°F).
 
• The process involves the **decomposition of sugar molecules**, resulting in the formation of new compounds that provide the characteristic color and flavor of caramel.
 
• Caramelisation is a form of **non-enzymatic browning**, distinct from the Maillard reaction, which involves amino acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maillard Reaction**:

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that gives browned foods their distinctive flavor.
 
• Unlike caramelisation, it involves proteins and occurs at lower temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation**:
 
 
• It is a process where a solid forms from a solution during a chemical reaction.
 
• It is not related to the heating of sugar.
 
 
 
• **Neutralisation**:
 
 
• It is a chemical reaction in which an acid and a base react to form water and a salt.
 
• This reaction is not related to the process of caramelisation.
 
 
 
• **Enzymatic Browning**:
 
 
• It occurs in fruits and vegetables, involving enzymes such as polyphenol oxidase.
 
• It is different from non-enzymatic browning processes like caramelisation and the Maillard reaction.

questions.question: The number of Rajya Sabha members to be elected from each State of India has been fixed by the _______ Schedule of the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the states and union territories.
 
• Rajya Sabha, also known as the Council of States, is the upper house of India's Parliament.
 
• The Fourth Schedule specifies the number of Rajya Sabha members to be elected from each state and union territory.
 
• This allocation is based on the population of each state and union territory.
 
• The total number of members in the Rajya Sabha is capped at 250, including 12 members nominated by the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha:**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution.
 
• One-third of its members retire every two years, ensuring continuity.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies and Electoral college for Union Territories.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• The Fourth Schedule has been amended multiple times to reflect changes in the allocation of seats based on census data.
 
• Such amendments ensure that representation in the Rajya Sabha remains proportionate to the population of states and union territories.
 
 
 
• **Representation:**
 
 
• States with larger populations have more seats in the Rajya Sabha compared to smaller states.
 
• Union territories with smaller populations have fewer seats, with some having only one seat.
 
 
 
• **Nominated Members:**
 
 
• In addition to elected members, the President of India nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• These nominated members are chosen for their contributions to art, literature, science, and social services.

questions.question: According to Census 2011 of India, which Union Territory has the second highest percentage of urban population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandigarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, Chandigarh has the second highest percentage of urban population among Union Territories in India.
 
• Chandigarh has an urban population percentage of 97.25%.
 
• Chandigarh is a city and a union territory in India that serves as the capital of the two neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• The city was designed by the Swiss-French modernist architect, Le Corbusier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi**:

 
 
• Delhi has the highest percentage of urban population among Union Territories, with 97.50% as per Census 2011.
 
• It is the capital territory of India and a significant cultural, political, and commercial center.
 
 
 
• **Puducherry**:
 
 
• Puducherry, formerly known as Pondicherry, has an urban population of 68.33%.
 
• It comprises four coastal regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam.
 
 
 
• **Daman and Diu**:
 
 
• Daman and Diu had an urban population percentage of 75.16% as per the 2011 Census.
 
• In January 2020, Daman and Diu were merged with Dadra and Nagar Haveli to form the new union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories in India**:
 
 
• Union Territories (UTs) are regions governed directly by the Central Government of India.
 
• As of 2023, India has 8 Union Territories, which include Delhi, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Ladakh, and Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.question: As per the treaty of Purandar, how many forts were surrendered by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to Mughals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Treaty of Purandar, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj agreed to surrender 23 forts to the Mughal Empire.
 
• This treaty was signed on June 11, 1665, between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Raja Jai Singh I, who was representing the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• The forts surrendered included strategically significant ones like Purandar, Rudramal, Lohgad, and Mahuli.
 
• The treaty also required Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to pay a compensation of 400,000 huns to the Mughal Empire.
 
• In return, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was allowed to retain 12 forts along with an area worth an annual income of 100,000 huns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Treaty of Purandar (1665)**: This was a pivotal agreement between the Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and the Mughal Empire, marking a temporary halt in hostilities.
 
• **Raja Jai Singh I**: He was a Rajput general serving under Emperor Aurangzeb, who played a key role in negotiating the Treaty of Purandar with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
 
• **Forts**: These were crucial military assets in medieval India, often serving as administrative centers and military strongholds.
 
• **Compensation Payment**: The payment of 400,000 huns by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to the Mughals was a significant financial burden, reflecting the substantial economic costs of the treaty.
 
• **Strategic Retreat**: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's decision to surrender the forts was seen as a strategic retreat to buy time and consolidate his forces for future resistance against the Mughals.

questions.question: At what temperature do Celsius and Fahrenheit scales have the same value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-40ºC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Celsius and Fahrenheit scales have the same value at **-40 degrees**.
 
• The formula to convert Celsius to Fahrenheit is F = (C × 9/5) + 32.
 
• At -40 degrees Celsius, the formula becomes F = (-40 × 9/5) + 32, which simplifies to F = -40.
 
• This convergence is due to the way the two scales are constructed, with different zero points and scaling factors.
 
• Understanding this convergence can help in various scientific calculations and temperature conversions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Celsius Scale:**

 
 
• Developed by Anders Celsius in 1742.
 
• Based on the freezing point (0ºC) and boiling point (100ºC) of water at 1 atmospheric pressure.
 
• Widely used in most countries around the world.
 
 
 
• **Fahrenheit Scale:**
 
 
• Developed by Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit in 1724.
 
• Based on the freezing point of brine (a mixture of water, ice, and salt) at 0°F and the human body temperature at approximately 96°F (later adjusted to 98.6°F).
 
• Commonly used in the United States and its territories.
 
 
 
• **Kelvin Scale:**
 
 
• Developed by William Thomson, 1st Baron Kelvin, in 1848.
 
• An absolute temperature scale starting at absolute zero (0 K), where all molecular motion stops.
 
• Used primarily in scientific research and applications.
 
 
 
• **Absolute Zero:**
 
 
• The lowest possible temperature where nothing could be colder and no heat energy remains in a substance.
 
• Absolute zero is 0 K on the Kelvin scale, -273.15ºC on the Celsius scale, and -459.67ºF on the Fahrenheit scale.

questions.question: Where does the cash grants in aid from foreign countries are classified?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Non-tax revenue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cash grants in aid from foreign countries** are classified as **non-tax revenue**.
 
• Non-tax revenue includes all revenue that the government receives other than taxes.
 
• Examples of non-tax revenue include grants, fees, fines, and dividends from public sector enterprises.
 
• Cash grants are typically given by foreign countries to support various sectors such as education, health, infrastructure, and disaster relief.
 
• Non-tax revenue is crucial for the government as it provides additional funds for public expenditure without imposing taxes on citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure:**

 
 
• Refers to the expenses incurred for the day-to-day functioning of the government and maintenance of infrastructure.
 
• Includes salaries, pensions, interest payments, and subsidies.
 
• Does not result in the creation of assets.
 
 
 
• **Capital Receipts:**
 
 
• Include loans, disinvestment, and other receipts that create liabilities or reduce assets.
 
• Are used for capital expenditure which leads to asset creation.
 
 
 
• **Tax Revenue:**
 
 
• Comprises taxes collected by the government such as income tax, GST, customs duty, and excise duty.
 
• It is the primary source of revenue for the government.
 
 
 
• **Non-tax Revenue Sources:**
 
 
• Interest receipts, dividends, and profits from public sector enterprises.
 
• Fees and fines collected by various government departments.
 
• Grants and donations from foreign countries and international organizations.

questions.question:

 Column A (Name of the Awardee)
 Column B (Dance form)

__

• Siba Prasad Das is renowned for his work in **Chhau Dance**.

questions.question: What is the full form of INSAT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Satellite System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **INSAT** stands for **Indian National Satellite System**, a series of multipurpose geostationary satellites commissioned by ISRO.
 
• The primary objective of INSAT is to cater to telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and search and rescue operations.
 
• INSAT was established in 1983, marking a significant step in India's space program.
 
• These satellites are a collaborative effort between ISRO and the Department of Space, Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geostationary Satellites:**

 
 
• These are satellites that orbit the Earth at a fixed position relative to the surface, providing consistent coverage over a specific area.
 
• They are typically used for communication, weather forecasting, and surveillance.
 
 
 
• **ISRO:**
 
 
• The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is the space agency of the Government of India, responsible for the country's space program.
 
• ISRO's primary objective is to advance space technology and use its applications for various national tasks.
 
 
 
• **Telecommunications:**
 
 
• INSAT satellites play a crucial role in providing telecommunication services, including telephone and data transmission.
 
• They support the infrastructure for mobile networks, internet services, and direct-to-home (DTH) television.
 
 
 
• **Meteorology:**
 
 
• INSAT satellites are equipped with meteorological payloads to monitor weather patterns and provide crucial data for weather forecasting.
 
• They help in tracking cyclones, assessing rainfall, and predicting natural disasters.

questions.question: Under the influence of the Greeks, which of the following art styles flourished in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhar art style is heavily influenced by Greek art, particularly after the conquests of Alexander the Great.
 
• This art form flourished primarily in the regions of present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan during the 1st to 5th centuries CE.
 
• Gandhar art is characterized by intricate carvings, realistic human figures, and the use of motifs such as Greek gods and mythological beings.
 
• The most significant contributions of Gandhar art are the numerous sculptures of the Buddha, which exhibit a blend of Indian and Greek artistic elements.
 
• The Gandhar style played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism through its expressive and detailed representations of the Buddha and Buddhist narratives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kushan Empire:** The Gandhar region was under the control of the Kushan Empire, which facilitated the synthesis of Greek and Indian art forms.
 
• **Iconography:** Gandhar art is noted for introducing the iconic representation of the Buddha in human form, prior to which he was represented by symbols.
 
• **Materials Used:** Artists in the Gandhar region commonly used materials like grey schist and stucco for their sculptures and architectural decorations.
 
• **Architectural Influence:** The architectural style of Gandhar includes elements like Corinthian columns and acanthus leaf decorations, reflecting Greek influence.
 
• **Spread of Gandhar Art:** Gandhar art significantly influenced the art and culture of Central Asia, China, and other parts of Asia through the Silk Road.

questions.concept: Foundation of the Indian National Congress
questions.question: In which year was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1885**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in **1885**.
 
• The session took place in Bombay (now Mumbai) from **28-31 December 1885**.
 
• The session was presided over by **W.C. Bonnerjee**.
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded by **Allan Octavian Hume**, a retired British civil servant.
 
• This session marked the beginning of the organized national movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress**:

 
 
• The Indian National Congress was established on **28 December 1885**.
 
• The primary objective of the Congress was to obtain a greater share in government for educated Indians.
 
• It played a significant role in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
 
 
• **W.C. Bonnerjee**:
 
 
• Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee was the first president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was a prominent Indian barrister and one of the founding members of the Congress.
 
 
 
• **Allan Octavian Hume**:
 
 
• Allan Octavian Hume was a British civil servant and one of the founders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of the Indian National Congress".
 
 
 
• **Bombay (Mumbai)**:
 
 
• Bombay, now known as Mumbai, was the location for the first session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Mumbai is the capital city of the Indian state of Maharashtra and the financial, commercial, and entertainment capital of India.
